problem: Learned planners for unknown-environment exploration and point-goal navigation either use graph-only representations that miss fine-grained occupancy-map details, or use map prediction (a single deterministic layout) only to feed conventional planners, so prediction and learned planning are rarely integrated.
motivation: Humans plan with cognitive maps, reasoning over plausible layouts of unseen space. Planning under partial belief needs an estimate of information gain and uncertainty. Multiple plausible layout hypotheses could give a learned planner global structural priors and reduce myopic behavior.
key_idea: Use a lightweight conditional WGAN inpainter with multiple layout-conditioning vectors to generate several plausible layouts, average them into per-node uncertainty on a predicted graph, and feed that graph to an SAC-trained graph-attention planner for exploration and point-goal navigation.
insight: Multiple diverse predictions, even if individually inaccurate, give useful uncertainty priors, but they only help when the planner is uncertainty-aware. Inpaint+TARE (predictions treated as ground truth) is worse than all baselines (372.3 vs 306.4 exploration length), whereas the learned planner gains 7.0% over ARiADNE+. More predictions (1→4→7) improve performance with saturating gains, and the predictions also help zero-shot on out-of-distribution floor plans and Gazebo environments.
method: Conditional generative inpainting: a WGAN-GP generator (<0.35M params) takes the occupancy belief, an unknown-region mask and a layout-type conditioning vector (room/tunnel/outdoor), and is trained with adversarial, L1, spatially-discounted L1 (γ=0.95) and Dice losses, after a 10k-iteration reconstruction warmup and 490k adversarial iterations.

Layout uncertainty via conditioning vectors: a set of one-hot, soft one-hot and uniform vectors (|Z|=7 in training, 4 at test) yields multiple binarized, morphologically cleaned predictions. Their average gives a per-pixel free-space probability (Bernoulli).

Predicted-layout graph: nodes are uniformly placed (9 px spacing, 26 px connection radius, ≤25 neighbors) over known and predicted free space, with attributes (coordinates, known/predicted flag s, mean free probability p, frontier utility u, guidepost g on the shortest path to the nearest frontier). Navigation adds a goal direction vector.

Graph-attention policy: an encoder of stacked masked self-attention layers over the graph and a decoder that uses the current node as query over its neighbors. The single-head attention scores serve directly as the policy over next-waypoint neighbors.

Privileged critic: it has the same architecture as the policy and takes the ground-truth graph with prediction probabilities, outputting Q-values. It is trained with discrete SAC, with rewards for completion and travel-distance penalty, plus frontier discovery (exploration) or goal proximity (navigation).

Training pipeline: the inpainter is trained on 3000 TARE-explored procedural Dungeon maps (room/tunnel/outdoor) and then frozen. The exploration planner is trained on 6000 maps and the navigation planner on 2000 maps (250×250 grid, 40 px sensing range).

setting.backbone: Conditional WGAN-GP inpainter (<0.35M params) + graph-attention policy/critic network trained with SAC (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Inpainter: 3000 procedurally generated Dungeon maps (room/tunnel/outdoor), snapshots taken every +10% exploration rate with TARE. Planner: 6000 maps for exploration, 2000 maps for navigation, in simulation.
setting.observation: 2D occupancy-grid belief from simulated LiDAR (40 px range), converted to a graph; real robot uses Livox Mid-360 3D LiDAR + Octomap
setting.action_space: discrete choice of neighboring graph node (waypoint)
setting.simulator: Custom 2D grid simulator (Dungeon maps), KTH floor plans, Gazebo
setting.privileged: Critic uses ground-truth graph during training only; none at test time

numbers_note: The KTH floor-plan results and the number-of-predictions ablation are given only in figures, so no numeric values are available. There is no standard VLN or ObjectNav benchmark; benchmarks are custom exploration/navigation setups reporting travel length.
results: CogniPlan reduces exploration travel length by 7.0% versus ARiADNE+ (306.4 vs 329.3 average) and 17.7% versus Inpaint+TARE. For navigation, it reduces travel length by 12.5% versus CA and 3.9% versus Inpaint+A*, and slightly beats D*Lite (222.1 vs 224.6). It also outperforms TARE/HPHS/DSVP in Gazebo, and works on hardware without retraining.
limitations: The inpainting model requires a fixed-size occupancy map input, which leaves a domain gap in out-of-distribution deployment.
The generator is frozen during planner training (one-way pipeline), so there is no joint or online adaptation, and the conditioning vector set is hand-designed.
Each new prediction triggers a full rebuild of the graph, which is a replanning computation bottleneck.
